mx.teacher_note: A destarched green leaf supplied with water and carbon dioxide will form starch in darkness.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Making starch produces the carbon dioxide around the leaf.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Even with carbon dioxide supplied, the half inside the bottle will not form starch.

intelligence.enrichment: A leaf part supplied with water, sunlight, and chlorophyll forms starch only if carbon dioxide is available; when carbon dioxide is unavailable, that leaf part does not turn blue-black with iodine. Carbon dioxide available to a sunlit green leaf part -> starch forms; carbon dioxide unavailable -> starch does not form. The learner correctly applies this rule: A leaf part supplied with water, sunlight, and chlorophyll forms starch only if carbon dioxide is available; when carbon dioxide is unavailable, that leaf part does not turn blue-black with iodine. A leaf inside a bottle still gets enough air because the plant is outside, so carbon dioxide availability does not affect starch formation.
